terms.definition: An open-source AI agent that runs locally on your machine, connecting messaging channels (WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram) to executable skills via natural language triggers.
terms.example: Typing 'how are my EC2 instances?' in WhatsApp triggers OpenClaw to run the aws-health skill and return a status report.

terms.definition: A folder containing a SKILL.md (agent instructions) and one or more scripts. The agent reads SKILL.md to decide when to invoke the skill and what scripts to run.
terms.example: The aws-health skill folder contains SKILL.md and scripts/aws.ts — the agent runs aws.ts when you ask about AWS infrastructure.

terms.definition: A markdown file inside a skill folder, read by the OpenClaw agent to understand the skill's name, description, and when to activate it. Not documentation for humans — instructions for the AI.
terms.example: SKILL.md contains: 'name: aws-health, description: Check health of AWS EC2 instances and ECS clusters...'

terms.definition: The modern modular AWS Software Development Kit for JavaScript/TypeScript. Packages are split by service (e.g., @aws-sdk/client-ec2) so you only import what you need.
terms.example: import { EC2Client, DescribeInstancesCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-ec2'

terms.definition: AWS's virtual server service. You launch, configure, and run virtual machines (instances) in the cloud, paying for compute time used.
terms.example: A t3.micro EC2 instance running a Node.js web server in us-east-1.

terms.definition: AWS's fully managed container orchestration service. You define tasks (Docker containers), group them into services, and run them on clusters of EC2 or Fargate.
terms.example: An ECS service running 3 replicas of a Python Flask app inside a cluster named 'production'.

terms.definition: AWS's observability service for collecting metrics, logs, and events from AWS resources. Used by the aws-health skill to pull CPU utilization data (15-minute average) for EC2 instances.
terms.example: GetMetricStatistics fetches CPU utilization for an EC2 instance over the last 5 minutes.

terms.definition: AWS's service for controlling who (users, roles, services) can do what (actions) on which AWS resources. Used to create a least-privilege user for OpenClaw.
terms.example: An IAM user with only ec2:DescribeInstances and cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics — nothing else.

terms.definition: A security principle: grant only the minimum permissions needed to perform a task. For OpenClaw, this means read-only access to EC2, ECS, and CloudWatch only.
terms.example: Instead of ec2:*, grant only ec2:DescribeInstances and ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus.

terms.definition: Accessing AWS services via API using an Access Key ID and Secret Access Key, rather than through the AWS Management Console. Required for OpenClaw's AWS SDK calls.
terms.example: The aws-health skill uses ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY environment variables to authenticate API calls.

terms.definition: A TypeScript runner that executes .ts files directly without a separate compilation step. Used in the aws-health skill to run TypeScript scripts at runtime.
terms.example: Running 'npx tsx scripts/aws.ts ec2' executes the EC2 health check directly.

terms.definition: An EC2 API call that returns metadata about your EC2 instances: IDs, types, names (from tags), and current state (running/stopped/terminated).
terms.example: DescribeInstances returns a list of Reservations, each containing one or more instance objects.

terms.definition: An EC2 API call that returns the system and instance status checks for each instance — whether AWS's underlying hardware and the instance OS are healthy.
terms.example: Status: ok means both system and instance checks passed. impaired means a check failed.

terms.definition: A CloudWatch API call that retrieves data points for a specific metric (e.g., CPUUtilization) for a resource over a defined time period and granularity.
terms.example: Get average CPU utilization for instance i-12345 over the last 15 minutes (900-second period) — as used in the aws-health skill.

terms.definition: A legacy EC2 grouping returned by DescribeInstances. A reservation wraps one or more instances that were launched together. NOT the same as Reserved Instances pricing.
terms.example: response.Reservations[0].Instances[0] — you must iterate through reservations to get to instance data.

terms.definition: The ability to activate a skill using free-form text in plain English (or any language), rather than a rigid command syntax. OpenClaw maps natural language to the right skill via SKILL.md descriptions.
terms.example: 'check aws', 'how are my instances?', 'is production healthy?' can all trigger the same aws-health skill.

terms.definition: An API by Meta that allows businesses and developers to send/receive WhatsApp messages programmatically. OpenClaw connects to your own WhatsApp number — not a WhatsApp Business account — via this API.
terms.example: Messages you send to your own WhatsApp are intercepted by OpenClaw, processed, and replied to automatically.

terms.definition: An AWS service that provides programmatic access to service health events — outages, maintenance, and scheduled changes affecting your AWS account. Reports at service level, not per-instance level.
terms.example: AWS Health might report 'EC2 experiencing elevated error rates in us-east-1' — a regional service event.

terms.definition: A protocol for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources. OpenClaw skills are conceptually similar to MCP tools — both define capabilities an AI agent can invoke.
terms.example: An MCP tool 'get_weather(city)' is analogous to an OpenClaw skill that runs a weather script when you ask about weather.

terms.definition: An AI system that can take actions autonomously — reading context, choosing which tool or skill to use, executing it, and returning results — rather than just generating text responses.
terms.example: OpenClaw is an agent: it reads your WhatsApp message, identifies the right skill, runs the script, and sends back the infrastructure report.

terms.definition: A temporary credential used with AWS STS (Security Token Service) when using assumed roles or MFA-authenticated sessions. Optional for basic IAM user access but required for role-based access.
terms.example: If using AWS SSO or cross-account roles, you need SESSION_TOKEN in addition to ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY.

terms.definition: A logical grouping of compute resources (EC2 instances or Fargate capacity) that ECS tasks and services run on. The aws-health skill lists all clusters and reports their service/task counts.
terms.example: A cluster named 'production' running 5 services with 20 total tasks across 3 EC2 instances.

terms.definition: A running instance of a task definition — one or more containers executing together. The aws-health skill counts running tasks per service to detect unhealthy or stopped tasks.
terms.example: A task running containers for a web server and a log sidecar together in the same task definition.
